question:
Three cards are drawn successively without replacement from a pack of 52 playing cards. Find the probability that
(a) all three cards are spades,
(b) the first card is a spade, the second is a heart, and the third is a diamond.
explanation:
There are 52 cards: 13 spades, 13 hearts, 13 diamonds, and 13 clubs.

(a) All three are spades:
$P(\text{1st is spade}) = \frac{13}{52}$
$P(\text{2nd is spade | 1st spade}) = \frac{12}{51}$
$P(\text{3rd is spade | first two are spades}) = \frac{11}{50}$

So, $P = \frac{13}{52} \times \frac{12}{51} \times \frac{11}{50} = \frac{13 \times 12 \times 11}{52 \times 51 \times 50} = \frac{1716}{132600} = \frac{143}{11050}$

(b) First is spade, second is heart, third is diamond:
$P_1 = \frac{13}{52}$
After spade drawn: 51 left. Hearts: 13 still.
$P_2 = \frac{13}{51}$
After spade, then heart: Diamonds left: 13, remaining cards: 50.
$P_3 = \frac{13}{50}$

$P = \frac{13}{52} \times \frac{13}{51} \times \frac{13}{50} = \frac{13^3}{52 \times 51 \times 50} = \frac{2197}{132600}$
